title: Ideal-power annihilation of a supported coherent module on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is Noetherian: locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests). Modules are sheaves on the small etale ringed site; quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. The support $\operatorname{Supp}(F)$ is the set of points with nonzero geometric stalk, in the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For an ideal sheaf $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and a module $M$, $I^nM$ is the submodule locally generated by products of $n$ sections of $I$ and one of $M$, with $I^0M=M$. Let $F$ be coherent and $I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Write $Z(I)\subseteq|X|$ for the closed subset whose inverse image on every affine etale chart is the zero locus of the ideal on that chart. Then $$\operatorname{Supp}(F)\subseteq Z(I)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there exists }n\geq0\text{ with }I^nF=0.$$ The expression $I^nF=0$ means the zero submodule sheaf.

source.place: Tag 07UK, lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf, statement (closed subspace expressed by its ideal zero locus).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] to the given quasi-coherent ideal $I$. It supplies a closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ whose defining ideal $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ is exactly $I$, and whose base change to an etale scheme chart has defining ideal $I$ restricted to that chart.

source.place: Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals, inverse construction and inverse-image paragraph.

proof.text: The subset $|i|(|Z|)$ is $Z(I)$. Indeed take the disjoint-affine atlas of [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover], which is surjective on point classes. On each affine component $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$, Step 1 identifies $Z\times_XT$ with the closed subscheme defined by the restricted ideal $J$. The affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] gives $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$, whose point image is $V(J)$: primes of $A/J$ are exactly primes of $A$ containing $J$. A point of $T$ lies over $|Z|$ exactly when its field-valued map factors through $Z$ after a field extension, equivalently when $J$ maps to zero in its residue field, by the factorization criterion in [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence]. Thus the inverse images of $|i|(|Z|)$ and $Z(I)$ on every atlas component agree. Surjectivity on point classes gives the asserted equality.

source.place: Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals, field-valued factorization criterion and base change; Tag 07UK uses the resulting set-theoretic closed subset.

proof.text: The powers in the item agree with the recursively defined products in [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power]. Both give $F$ at exponent zero. If the products of $n$ ideal sections acting on a section of $F$ generate the $n$th term locally, multiplying a local finite sum of these generators by a section of $I$ gives a sum of products of $n+1$ ideal sections. Conversely each such product is a section of $I$ times a generator of the $n$th term. Hence both definitions give the same submodule sheaf at exponent $n+1$, proving the equality by induction.

source.place: Tag 07UK, lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf, interpretation of the ideal-power product; elementary associativity and distributivity.

proof.text: Apply the support/annihilation equivalence of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power] to $X,F,i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. Its hypotheses are precisely the given Noetherianity and coherence; $Z$ need not be reduced. Its ideal is $I$ by Step 1, its closed point subset is $Z(I)$ by Step 2, and its product submodules are those of the item by Step 3. Substitution into that equivalence proves both implications with the same range $n\geq0$.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_support_power_ideal_kills {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : ∀ (U V : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (b : yoneda.obj V ⟶ X.obj.obj), IsAffine U.left → IsAffine V.left → CompactSpace (Point (Limits.pullback a b))) (F : X.Modules) (hFqc : F.IsQuasicoherent) (hFcoh : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (X.etaleForget.obj T).toRingedSpace ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj F)) (I : X.Modules) (i : I ⟶ SheafOfModules.unit X.structureSheaf) [Mono i] (hI : I.IsQuasicoherent) : (∀ (T : X.EtaleSite), IsAffine (X.etaleForget.obj T) → ∀ x : X.etaleForget.obj T, ¬ Subsingleton (((X.schemeRestriction T).obj F).presheaf.stalk x) → ∀ a ∈ idealSectionImage i T, (X.etaleForget.obj T).Γevaluation x a = 0) ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, idealPowerSubsheafSections i F (fun _ ↦ Set.univ) n T = {0}
lean.note: Arbitrary ideal subsheaf is a monomorphism into the existing unit module. Support in its zero locus is expanded on all affine etale charts by vanishing of ideal sections in residue fields. Chartwise ordinary stalk vanishing equals geometric stalk vanishing for quasi-coherent modules. Ideal-power section subsets are the existing locally generated products owned by def-sfb-space-ideal-power-products in the existing Artin-Rees module; equality with {0} on every test means the zero submodule sheaf. No additional choice of closed subspace is assumed.
